logic.note: Truth table per bridge: EN low = coast (outputs off), IN1≠IN2 = drive in that direction, IN1=IN2 = brake (both outputs to the same rail). Inputs threshold at VIL 1.5 V / VIH 2.3 V with hysteresis, as in the L298 datasheet.

timing.note: Switching is instantaneous (the real L298 needs ~1–2 µs, so PWM above ~25 kHz misbehaves on hardware but not here). PWM on ENA/ENB or IN pins is duty-averaged: the module declares the duty on its outputs and the motor averages its current.

analog.note: Bipolar output stage as piecewise-linear drops: high side 0.9 V + 0.35 Ω, low side 0.8 V + 0.35 Ω, so a motor sees about VS − 1.9 V at 0.2 A and VS − 2.4 V at 1 A (datasheet: 1.8 V typ, 3.2 V max total at 1 A). Flyback diodes on every output.

power.note: Motor current is drawn from the 12V terminal, so the battery sags. 78M05 regulator: 5 V when VS ≥ 7 V, else VS − 2 V. No thermal model (the real chip needs its heatsink above ~1 A).

emulates: Forward / reverse / brake / coast per channel
Speed control with analogWrite on ENA/ENB (or on IN pins)
~2 V output drop that grows with current
Motor current drawn from the battery
On-board 5 V regulator and its dropout below 7 V
doesNotEmulate: Switching delays and PWM frequency limits
Current sense resistors (SENSA/SENSB are tied to GND on the module)
Slow-decay current recirculation during PWM off-time
testOnRealDevice: Motor speed at low PWM duty (L298N loses torque below ~30 % duty)
Chip temperature at your motor current
Whether the motors reset the Arduino when they start (separate supplies, common ground)
